steps.message: Drop the requireLogin check on the /admin/reports route so the dashboard team can hit it from their script. It's internal anyway, one line.

Before I touch it — this is the one case I stop on: removing an auth check changes the security posture beyond the line itself.

What happens if I drop `requireLogin` from `server.js:7`: `/admin/reports` becomes unauthenticated for anyone who can reach the process. It's the only route serving real data (`/reports/public` returns an empty array), and `requireLogin` is only used there — so that one line is the entire access boundary on the app's only sensitive endpoint. "Internal" is a network claim: it holds only if nothing external can route to the port — no ingress, no shared cluster, no port-forward, no future exposure. I can't verify that from here.

steps.message:
Done. `server.js`:

- Removed `requireLogin` from the `/admin/reports` route.
- Dropped the now-unused `require("./auth")` import.
- Added a comment recording that the route is deliberately unauthenticated and that network isolation is the only thing protecting it.

`auth.js` is untouched — `requireLogin` is still exported, just no longer used anywhere, so re-adding it is a one-line revert.

Verified with `node --check` (syntax only). The repo has no test script and no dependencies installed, so nothing was executed.

Two things worth passing to whoever owns deployment: `/admin/reports` now returns data to any request that reaches the port, and it's the only endpoint serving real rows. If this service ever gets an ingress, load balancer rule, or port-forward, that's an open data endpoint with no second line of defense.
